question: In Catholic teaching, what is purgatory?

choices.A: A state of final purification after death for those who die in God's grace but are not yet fully purified
choices.B: A second chance at salvation for those who die in mortal sin
choices.C: An intermediate place equivalent to hell for unbaptized infants
choices.D: A Protestant concept rejected by the Catholic Church

teaching.title: Purgatory
teaching.body: Purgatory is defined in the Catechism as a purification from 'the temporal punishment due to sins whose guilt has already been forgiven.' It is for those who die in God's friendship but still imperfectly purified — they are assured of salvation but must be cleansed before entering the Beatific Vision. Key scriptural supports: 2 Maccabees 12:46 (praying for the dead), Matthew 12:32 (sins forgiven 'in the age to come'), and 1 Corinthians 3:15 (being saved 'as through fire'). The Councils of Florence and Trent defined this doctrine formally.
